description: NEGATIVE CONTROL for tests/hillside_corpus.cpp (PL.native-grading-plan-call), made from core's conformance/hillside/pads.json at the pin by the builder's gen-hillside-negative.mjs: the contract's wallMaxM moved to 1.6, one true case, six cases whose expected answer (or engine list) is wrong, and a control that changes nothing. hillside_corpus_negative passes only when the runner reports every one of them and fails the run.

contract.reportLine: N grading patches not applied (only when N > 0)
contract.overlapSlopeRule: On the world lattice (i, j) × overlapSlopeLatticeM, a point covered (padFlatOutside < reach) by two or more of the plan's pads, at least one a hillside pad, is read: the point function's gradient (dividers included) by central differences of overlapSlopeDiffM, only when the four difference points lie in the same grading part of every covering pad and on the same side of every divider. A slope over standMaxGradient + overlapSlopeTolerance charges every pair of its covering pads of which at least one is a hillside pad (a hillside pad and a default pad included; two default pads never). Charged pairs are divided by neighbourWallRule; each pair still charged after that is one finding "pads <id> and <id>: where their grading regions overlap, the graded ground off the walls is steeper than <standMaxDeg>°", pairs ascending by id, after the pads' own findings.
contract.neighbourWallRule: Walls between neighbours (§5): each pair overlapSlopeRule charges on the blended ground, taken ascending by id, is divided by a straight retaining wall. The candidate lines are separating lines of the two lots (fit rectangles): for each axis (the lower id's away and across axes, the other's, then the centre-to-centre axis; each oriented from the lower id's centre toward the other's, a square axis as given; an axis the same as an earlier kept one, or along which the lots overlap by more than 1e-9 m, left out) the line square to it at the middle of the gap between the lots' projections, widest gap first, axis order on a tie: one wall on each such line first (stripHalfM 0), then, for each line whose gap is over 1e-9 m and in the same order, a shared terrace filling the gap (stripHalfM half the gap). With s the signed distance past the line toward the other pad and h = stripHalfM, the lower id grades only s < h and the other only s >= -h (a pad on its far side is left out of the blend); on the shared terrace -h <= s < h the ground is the mean of the two blends, each with one of the pair left out. A default member is sized as a hillside pad. The first candidate is kept with which no dividing wall (of any division) steps over wallMaxM; if none is kept the pair stays blended and any promotion is undone. Each pair is tried once; the rule is read again on the divided ground until it charges no untried pair. A dividing wall is wall.<lower id>.nb.<other sourceFeatureId>.<n> (a shared terrace's edges .nb.<other>.1.<n> at s = -h and .nb.<other>.2.<n> at s = h): each line sampled across both pads' reach boxes at most gradedCellM apart (both ends), top and base read 1e-6 m either side; a pad's own wall line does not step past its dividing line, and is cut there 1e-4 m inside (on the arc, on a corner's arc).
contract.frame: Metres in core's relative frame over [0, terrainSize]²: an IR point p is the frame point p + terrainSize / 2; a height is n × verticalScale.value of the bilinear heightmap, nothing added.

replay.input: Each case's world is a World IR cut down to what the plan reads. For each engine in engines, build the grading plan; evaluate the point function at each of points, with otherPads (GradeLots' pads of the world's non-map lots, core TerrainPad shape) in the same pad set; and, when otherPads is given, check that set for a map lot stacked on GradeLots.
replay.compare: A refusal compares refused only. Otherwise pads, walls (every vertex), report, findings, points and padSet, numbers within tolerance (metres; awayX, awayZ and carryM within tolerance.unit), the rest exactly, object key sets included.
replay.controls: Each control is a case's answer with one thing changed. A checker must refuse every one: compare it with what the engine answers, and check the answer's own invariants (no wall vertex over wallMaxM; the report counts the pads and prints its line only when there are some; no wall on a default pad).
